newsitem.title: UK: UK farm minister says beef row cost UK 3.5 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK farm minister says beef row cost UK 3.5 bln stg.

text.p: Britain's Agriculture Minister, Douglas Hogg, facing a censure vote in parliament at 2200 GMT on Monday, said the crisis caused by fears of mad cow disease had cost Britain 3.5 billion stg so far.

Hogg, who is expected to survive the vote, called by the Labour opposition, rejected suggestions from farmers that he should have quit over his handling of the crisis, telling a BBC radio interviewer: "I'm not a resigning character."
Hogg, battling to end a European export ban on British beef exports, said things were "very much better" than a year ago, with beef consumption rising and farmers' incomes underpinned.

But he dismissed charges that a third of the dairy herd will be lost as part of a cull aimed at eradicating mad cow disease. "The figures are absolutely nonsense... The overall figures are very much lower than those," Hogg said.

Britain has promised its European partners a range of actions including the culling thousands of older cows, winning agreement at last June's European Union summit in June to move towards a lifting of the export ban.
But delays in getting the cull going has meant there has been little progress in lifting the export ban and an easing of the European embargo still seems to be months away.
Hogg said it was likely beef from Northern Ireland would benefit first from a lifting of the ban because more herds were grass fed and a cattle tracing scheme was already underway.

But he denied that the government was offering any special deals to nine Ulster Unionist members of parliament to ensure victory in Monday night's vote. The government is tied in parliament with all other parties and needs the backing of at least one more MP to ensure victory on Monday night. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
